thread:
maya (support): Heads up — multiple customers reporting p99 spikes on /v1/embeddings in eu-west after the midnight infra deploy. Seeing timeouts and 502s, some requests >5s. Anyone else seeing this?

alex_g (eng-runtime): I saw increased tail latency on the dashboard around 00:45 UTC. p95 up ~2x and p99 ~3-4x for embeddings routes. No change in request volume.

rohan_oncall (eng-sre): Paging in infra. Linking traces now. Can you paste a failing request ID?

maya (support): Example customer trace id: trace-0a9f3. Customer logs show repeated grpc reset errors to model host and occasional API 504.

deploy-bot: deploy finished: infra-cuda-driver-update v2.3.1 -> v2.4.0 at 00:30 UTC (eu-west).

juan_infra (eng-infra): That's the CUDA driver rollout for eu-west nodes. We rolled kernel+driver on the GPU node pool. Rolling back is possible but will cause brief allocation churn.

emma_eng (eng-platform): Correlating — nodes with the new driver show higher hostfs I/O wait and NVMe IO qdepth increased. Could be storage contention causing slower KV cache loads.

alex_g (eng-runtime): Runtime stack shows slower KV cache warmup on long contexts; the runtime waits for storage to populate KV pages for some embeddings models. If storage is contended, token generation stalls.

rohan_oncall (eng-sre): Repro steps from a node with the updated driver:
```
# run a steady embeddings workload
ab -n 1000 -c 20 "POST https://api.redwood.local/v1/embeddings"
# sample system snapshot
sudo bpftrace -e 'tracepoint:syscalls:sys_enter_read { @[comm] = count(); }' -c 'stress-ng --matrix 1'
iostat -x 1 5
```

alex_g (eng-runtime): Throwing a tiny trace of a slow request:
```
[2026-01-15T00:47:12Z] request_id=trace-0a9f3: kv_cache_miss -> fetch_shard(backend=nvme0n1p1, size=64MB) -> io_wait 312ms -> token_gen_pause
[2026-01-15T00:47:12Z] request_id=trace-0a9f3: backend_error: read_timeout after 3 retries
```

juan_infra (eng-infra): NVMe scheduler on those hosts is bfq with default qlen. After the driver update, we've seen IO stalls; kernel stats show I/O latency tail rising concurrently with driver install. Hypothesis: new driver touches host/kernel NVMe path causing scheduling interactions under heavy GPU DMA.

rohan_oncall (eng-sre): Initial mitigations proposal:
- Pause remaining CUDA driver rollouts in other regions (done).
- Move embeddings traffic to older driver node pool + autoscale to absorb load.
- Apply temporary io.scheduler change to noop on affected hosts and throttle background maintenance jobs.
- Add fallback model route (smaller quantized variant) for affected customers.

maya (support): Customers are asking about SLA credits and billing impact. We need a clear customer-facing note if we take a rollback.

emma_eng (eng-platform): I can add a quick route-level fallback to the quantized-embedding-v1 for the top 10 tenants and ensure responses remain consistent. That will reduce NVMe pressure because model footprints are smaller.

alex_g (eng-runtime): Also adding aggressive local KV caching (increase in-memory cache size by 30%) should reduce peeks to NVMe for hot prefixes. I can flip that on for eu-west only.

juan_infra (eng-infra): I started a targeted rollback of driver on 2/12 of the affected GPU hosts to validate. Reverting reduces IO stall events in ~10m window. Node still healthy.

deploy-bot: rollback started: infra-cuda-driver-update on eu-west pool subset (2 hosts) at 00:58 UTC.

rohan_oncall (eng-sre): Observed p99 dropping from 3.4s -> 0.9s in the small rollback window for embeddings. Logs show fewer "read_timeout" backend errors.

maya (support): Reporting back to customers: telling them we're mitigating by routing to fallback models and rolling back driver on affected nodes; will follow up when rollout plan is finalized.

alex_g (eng-runtime): Note: we still saw occasional 502s correlated with node restarts during rollback. Recommend draining instances gracefully and moving stateful workloads off before driver change.

juan_infra (eng-infra): Agreed. We'll pause full rollback until we have a safe drain/playbook. Next steps: run a canary revert with careful drain, monitor IO latency and p99 for 30m, then continue in waves.

rohan_oncall (eng-sre): Action items assigned:
- juan_infra: enact canary rollback + drain playbook (in progress)
- alex_g: enable extra in-memory KV cache for eu-west + monitor memory pressure
- emma_eng: enable route-level fallback for top-ten tenants and update customer notes
- maya: coordinate with CS on billing/SLA comms and collect affected tenant IDs

sre-bot: Incident annotation: severity=high, impacted=/v1/embeddings, regions=eu-west, pg=embedding-serving, start=1768007777

maya (support): Thanks team. I'll open a post-incident summary once we have final root cause. Leaving this thread open for updates. :thumbsup:

alex_g (eng-runtime): Preliminary root cause hypothesis to include in the postmortem: interaction between new CUDA driver and kernel NVMe path caused increased I/O tail under GPU DMA bursts leading to KV cache fetch stalls and p99 regressions. Candidate mitigations: driver revert, qdisc/scheduler tuning, larger in-memory KV cache, traffic fallbacks.

juan_infra (eng-infra): Will add kernel/sysfs tuning results to the incident doc after tests.

rohan_oncall (eng-sre): Monitoring shows p99 back to baseline after selective rollback + fallbacks. Continuing to observe for 1h.

maya (support): Closing loop with customers now; will flag any billing/credit asks. If anything changes I'll reopen.

emma_eng (eng-platform): Follow-up: we should add a pre-rollback checklist for driver updates that includes NVMe latency sampling and graceful drain steps.

maya (support): Noted. Thanks everyone.
